verdict.rationale: Proa documents incremental adoption at the route level: you proxy one route to Proa and leave the rest on Next.js or Rails. It also offers FFI calls from other runtimes, islands that hydrate only interactive parts, and scaffolds for full Axum apps. Adopting it for a sub-page fragment inside an existing page is only implied by the FFI and island features, not documented as a workflow. Missing for 10: an explicit guide for embedding Proa in part of an existing page, a documented migration path from fragment to full app, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can incrementally adopt the framework, scaling from a small part of a page up to a full application

citations.quote: Proxy one route to Proa, leave the rest on Next.js or Rails, then compare latency and cost in production.
Go Axum-native for Proa routing and responses, or call Proa over FFI from Node, Go, Python, Ruby, or Java.
Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
A minimal Axum-backed application with the core boundaries in place: proa new site hello-proa --yes
